depth_reference: interior water depth above ground-floor slab

standard_method.method: Hazus 6.1 default contents and inventory depth-damage functions for COM2
standard_method.citation: FEMA Hazus 6.1 flood contents and inventory damage functions (HazusFloodDamageFunctions_Hazus61.xlsx), contents and inventory sheets as published in NHERI SimCenter Damage and Loss Model Library
standard_method.value_basis: The same simulated item values as Waterline's contents loss (like for like): the Hazus inventory function for stock, the contents function for everything else; road vehicles and building fabric are excluded from both.
standard_method.statement: Against the Hazus-style figure on the same item values, at 1 ft ours is higher (2.2 times); at 2 ft ours is higher (2.5 times); at 4 ft ours is higher (1.8 times); at 6 ft ours is higher (1.5 times).
standard_method.why_shapes_differ: Hazus applies a building-average percentage from the first inch of water (16% of contents and 19% of inventory at 1 ft for COM2) and never reaches 100% (72% and 79% at 8 ft), because a building's contents include things stored above the water. Waterline prices only the items the survey saw, each from its own lowest vulnerable point: nothing is lost until the water reaches an item, and an item is a total loss once the water is its critical height above that point. In this building 73% of the surveyed contents value (at the middle of each range) sits in items whose lowest vulnerable part may be below 1 ft.

assumptions.text: Contents damage rises with water above each item's lowest vulnerable point: fraction = (depth - lowest point) / critical height, capped at 1. Critical height is set per value class and never exceeds the item's own height measured from the 3D scan. Low end: lowest point at the top of its range and the class's low value; high end: lowest point at the bottom of its range and the high value.
assumptions.source: Waterline method; totals sanity-checked against FEMA Hazus 6.1 contents curves (USACE Galveston, COM2/IND2)

assumptions.text: FIXTURE: placeholder depth-damage curve on improvement value, not a FEMA figure

Each item's replacement value is uncertain: lognormal, with the low and high ends of its value range as the 10th and 90th percentiles (the median is the geometric mean of the two). A range starting at $0 is spread evenly between $0 and the high end.

Items in the same value class share half of their value uncertainty (correlation 0.5 between log-values), because a class range set too high or too low is wrong for every item in it. Classes are independent of each other.
Each item's lowest vulnerable point is uncertain: spread evenly between the bottom and top of its measured or estimated height range, independently for each item.
Structure damage is uncertain between the Hazus low and high curves: spread evenly between them, at the same relative place at every depth within one draw, independent of contents.

4,000 simulated draws with a fixed seed (20261114), each evaluated at every depth, so results are reproducible and never fall as depth rises. Reported: the median and the 10th-90th percentile range (80% interval). Percentiles do not add up: the total's interval is not the sum of the contents and structure intervals.

Extreme bounds at 1 ft, for reference only: every item at the low end of its value range and the top of its height range gives contents $38,098, structure $93,000, total $131,098; every item at the high end and the bottom gives contents $180,260, structure $217,000, total $397,260. Both are far less likely than the 80% interval, because items do not all err the same way.
assumptions.source: Waterline method: the sums reported as the range before contracts v1.3
